A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NCMP/SINC-GCN research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive expansion and reformatting.

before.justification: V2 reports original UniqueSignature experiments, SINC-GCN benchmark results, and inference measurements in Tables II–IV, with experimental details in Appendix A.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds Exp/CExp experiments, aggregator sensitivity tests, structural analyses, and matched-width comparisons.

M1.justification: The NCMP message formulation and SINC-GCN architecture remain unchanged in Eqs. (12) and (15), including the shared neighborhood projection and two aggregators. New aggregator and width comparisons evaluate options within the existing design.

E1.justification: V3 extends synthetic coverage with Exp/CExp graph-satisfiability tasks involving 1-WL-indistinguishable graph pairs and minimally edge-corrupted, distinguishable pairs. UniqueSignature and all eight existing benchmark datasets and tasks remain.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds published CWN comparisons on ZINC and ogbg-molhiv, and GraphGPS comparisons on MNIST and CIFAR10. CWN was previously cited but not included in the reported comparison. Existing comparators remain, and Exp/CExp uses the established comparator set.

E3.justification: V3 adds an eight-layer, 64-hidden-unit Exp/CExp protocol, systematic aggregator controls across the eight benchmarks, matched-hidden-width comparisons, and evaluation by degree and clustering-coefficient quartiles. These substantially extend the evaluation design; the original UniqueSignature and main benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test expressivity on Exp/CExp, aggregator sensitivity in Table 5, performance across structural quartiles in Tables 7–9, and sensitivity under matched hidden widths in Table 10. The 'none' rows reproduce existing SIR-GCN results, and the earlier runtime analysis is retained as Appendix B.1.

E5.justification: Table 4 introduces Cohen's d effect sizes and explicitly defines the Welch-test reference as the best one-hop localized baseline. The stated five-seed reporting, means and standard deviations, and significance threshold of 0.05 are retained.

E6.justification: Every retained numerical row in the original UniqueSignature, benchmark, and runtime tables is unchanged. Substantial new results include Exp/CExp scores, CWN/GraphGPS entries, and aggregator, structural, and width analyses. Examples include SINC-GCN's 85.50±20.62% accuracy on Corrupt and floating-point failure with sum aggregation on WikiCS.

T1.justification: Section 3.1.1 adds a Jacobian-based expressivity argument, including the claimed full-rank cross-neighbor response and a rank-one attention derivation in footnote 2. V3 also adds permutation-equivariance reasoning for weight sharing and revises the background GAT formula in Eq. (7). The SINC-GCN formula, complexity expression, and acknowledgment of the 1-WL limitation already appeared in v2.

C1.justification: The three central contributions remain, but the abstract, introduction, and conclusion narrow the novelty framing from first formalizing neighborhood-contextualization to refining or adapting established set-based ideas. The main claims about the framework, its SINC-GCN instance, and practical performance remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations of aggregator instability, limited node-level benefits, and possible overfitting under increased parameter counts. It also develops task-tree and over-squashing explanations, expands applicability boundaries concerning biconnectivity, and proposes extending NCMP to LLM architectures.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds Exp/CExp implementation details, including AdamW, 500 epochs, batch size 20, and a validation-based learning-rate schedule. Earlier dataset splits, benchmark hyperparameters, A800 hardware, DGL/PyTorch implementation, and the code repository link are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.4 becomes a substantially expanded survey and positioning discussion covering subgraph GNNs, biconnectivity, graph Transformers, and graph foundation models. V3 explicitly connects NCMP to Deep Sets and other set-based methods, adds numerous relevant works, and removes earlier diffusion and subgraph-counting references.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, broader-GNN survey, conceptual-proof narrative, results discussion, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Related work and analyses gain detailed subsection structures, and the appendices move after the references.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from a two-column format to a single-column TMLR layout. Existing figures and tables are retypeset and relocated, comparator grouping and highlighting change, and six new tables display the added experiments and analyses.

improvement.justification: Exp/CExp tests and aggregator/width analyses add empirical support and reveal failure conditions absent from v2; clearer attribution to prior set-based methods also helps. The net gain is limited by new overstatements: Eq. (17) does not establish the claimed full rank, and Section 4.2.1 describes matched-width comparisons as unconfounded by parameter count although Appendix B.3 acknowledges increased parameters.
